commits.subject: base: Remove scoped value trim comments (#63259)

review.summary: Reviewed the single comment-only commit and its merged Joolia tree. No zero-origin adaptation is needed; existing HAMT and PersistentDict storage conversions remain intact.

commits.indexing_implications: The first-parent diff only deletes explanatory comments in `Compiler/test/verifytrim.jl`, `base/dict.jl:_keyvalueset`, and `base/hamt.jl:HashState`; it changes no expressions or behavior. The surrounding Joolia port was inspected: HAMT storage positions `i` are zero-origin (`init_hamt` writes `data[0]`, `entry_index` returns the zero-based count of preceding bitmap bits, and DFS starts at `i=0` and stops when `i >= length(data)`); `length` remains a count. `HashState.depth` and `shift` are traversal state, not collection positions. `ScopeStorage` is `PersistentDict{AbstractScopedValue,Any}`, so the trim test's values `1` and `2` are payload data, not indices. PersistentDict callers in `base/scope.jl`, `base/scopedvalues.jl`, `test/scopedvalues.jl`, `test/dict.jl`, and Compiler scoped-value tests were inspected.
commits.adaptations: None. The upstream change removes only comments documenting the static-trim specialization fix; the required Joolia behavior (`@nospecialize(val)`, pinned `HashState{K}` reconstruction, and zero-origin HAMT storage) remains present in the resulting tree. No source or regression-test edit is justified.
commits.tests: Recommended, not executed: run `make -C test dict-foundation` in both configured compile modes; run the Compiler `verifytrim` test through the normal test runner and check `scoped_trim_read() == 2` with no trim-verification errors; run the existing `test/dict.jl` PersistentDict/HAMT tests and `test/scopedvalues.jl` zero-origin scoped-binding cases, including the singleton HAMT and empty HAMT checks; then run `python3 contrib/ci/run.py --jobs 4` for the required gate. This review job intentionally ran no build or tests.
